paragraphs: 3D-DLP learns to describe a three-dimensional scene as a collection of compact entities. Its inputs are either images with depth information or voxel observations. Each learned latent particle represents a distinct scene entity and separates its position, bounding-box dimensions, and appearance into interpretable attributes. This gives the representation an explicit object-level organization.

The model learns through reconstruction: it encodes a scene into particles and then uses those particles to reconstruct the observation. This self-supervised objective also produces segmentation maps associated with individual particles. In experiments on simulated and real-world datasets, changing particle positions and decoding the result produces new scene configurations, demonstrating a form of controllable scene representation.

The authors also use these particles for robotic manipulation. They report improvements over baselines that omit explicit 3D information and baselines that process memory-intensive dense 3D inputs without object structure. The findings support combining spatial detail with compact entity-level organization, rather than treating representation size alone as the central design choice.
icml-2026-3d-dlp-self-supervised-3d-obje.tldr: 3D-DLP learns compact, editable 3D scene entities through reconstruction and improves downstream robotic manipulation.

paragraphs: UniMAGE addresses the planning stage of AI film creation, where writing a script and designing key images are often handled by separate models. The paper argues that these activities benefit from shared narrative and visual understanding. Its unified director turns user prompts into structured scripts and keyframes that can guide existing audio-video generation models in producing multi-shot films.

The architecture combines text and image generation through a Mixture-of-Transformers design. Training proceeds in two stages. First, interleaved text-image examples teach the model connections between script content and visual interpretation. Second, separate expert learning disentangles script writing from keyframe generation, aiming to preserve flexibility and creativity while drawing on the shared understanding learned earlier.

The authors report state-of-the-art performance among open-source models, with coherent scripts and visually consistent keyframes. These findings concern the director’s ability to organize a story and its visual presentation. The contribution is a coordinated planning interface for longer productions, with the final audio-video generation supplied by existing models.
icml-2026-bridging-your-imagination-with.tldr: UniMAGE jointly learns script writing and keyframe generation to help coordinate coherent, visually consistent multi-shot films.

paragraphs: A generated mini-game can look convincing while failing when someone tries to play it. This paper identifies scalable evaluation of that interactive behavior as a bottleneck in improving open-source code models. Static judgments can miss functional flaws, while agents that interact through a graphical interface can make evaluation computationally expensive.

ALIVE evaluates generated games using automated play, one-shot planning, and analysis of the page’s Document Object Model. The framework is designed to check interaction at high throughput. The authors report that it detects functional problems substantially better than static judges while operating orders of magnitude more efficiently than GUI agents in their experiments.

The evaluation system also supplies training information. It selects high-quality examples for supervised fine-tuning and provides a consistent reward signal for reinforcement learning. Using this pipeline, the authors train ALIVE-Coder and report superior interactive frontend generation. The broader contribution is connecting executable behavior to model improvement through an evaluator that can support training at scale.
icml-2026-bringing-code-alive-optimizing.tldr: ALIVE uses scalable automated gameplay evaluation to detect functional flaws and train better frontend code generators.

paragraphs: Light-field segmentation must assign semantic labels while accounting for both spatial content and information across viewing angles. Efficient linear-complexity models can struggle to preserve the geometry connecting those views. This paper focuses on epipolar plane image cues, which carry geometric information that can deteriorate when a model mixes spatial and angular features inadequately.

E²I-VRWKV introduces explicit geometric guidance into a Vision-RWKV backbone. Its attention block includes a generator that extracts disparity-sensitive biases, helping enforce consistency across views. A separate gating mechanism uses geometry to regulate the fusion of spatial and angular information. Together, these components make geometric structure an active part of feature integration.

On the UrbanLF benchmark, the authors report performance above other state-of-the-art methods, including 86.55% mean intersection-over-union on UrbanLF-Real. They also report a favorable balance between accuracy and linear computational efficiency. The result supports explicitly representing light-field geometry inside an efficient backbone, so scalability does not depend solely on generic feature mixing.
icml-2026-e-2-i-vrwkv-explicit-epi-repre.tldr: E²I-VRWKV adds explicit geometric guidance to an efficient light-field segmentation network, reaching 86.55% mIoU on UrbanLF-Real.

paragraphs: Assortment optimization asks which set of products a decision-maker should offer to maximize revenue. This paper studies that decision under a contextual multinomial logit choice model, while accounting for possible changes from the distribution represented in observed data. Its robust objective evaluates revenue against worst-case deviations within a specified set of possible distributions.

The authors consider three ways to define that uncertainty set: total variation, Kullback–Leibler divergence, and chi-square divergence. Each provides a different mathematical formulation of the distributions against which the assortment should be protected. The resulting optimization must handle both the product-selection decision and the additional worst-case distributional calculation.

The paper integrates strong duality results from distributionally robust optimization into tailored assortment procedures, obtaining polynomial-time algorithms for all three formulations. It also establishes sample complexity bounds for each. These contributions provide computational and theoretical foundations for learning robust assortments under the stated choice model, with protection defined by the selected ambiguity set rather than unrestricted distribution changes.
icml-2026-efficient-distributionally-rob.tldr: The paper develops polynomial-time algorithms and sample complexity bounds for robust assortment optimization under three distributional uncertainty measures.

paragraphs: Federated LoRA allows clients to fine-tune a language model using compact low-rank updates. Aggregating those updates by averaging their factors saves communication and preserves low rank, but can introduce errors. This paper identifies rotational misalignment as a major source: equivalent updates can use different internal coordinate orientations, so directly averaging their factors can cause destructive interference.

FedRot-LoRA aligns client factors with orthogonal transformations before aggregation. These transformations preserve the actual update represented by each pair of factors while reducing differences in their latent orientations. The method therefore addresses how updates are represented and combined without increasing communication cost or restricting the updates the model can express.

The authors provide convergence analysis examining factor-averaging error and show that alignment gives a tighter upper bound on that error. Experiments on language understanding and generation report consistent improvements over federated LoRA baselines across different data heterogeneity levels and ranks. The findings connect an aggregation problem to a correctable geometric mismatch between otherwise meaningful local updates.
icml-2026-fedrot-lora-mitigating-rotatio.tldr: FedRot-LoRA aligns the internal orientations of client updates before averaging, reducing aggregation error without extra communication.

paragraphs: FiSeR targets synthetic-image detectors that work well on familiar data but deteriorate on new domains. The authors observe that real and generated images remain partially separable in feature projections even when detection performance falls. This suggests that the classification head may rely too heavily on training-domain artifacts, motivating representations that support more transferable decisions.

The method combines two contrastive learning objectives. One separates natural images from synthetic images. The other preserves distinctions between synthetic images produced by different generators. This hierarchy encourages a representation to capture both the broad detection task and the diversity of synthetic sources, instead of collapsing all generated images into an undifferentiated group.

Training on WildFake produces a reported average AUROC gain of 10.22 across four cross-domain evaluations under the same settings as DIRE. The paper also studies adaptation by freezing the backbone and fitting an SVM with ten labeled examples per class. Averaged across twelve detectors, that procedure improves AUROC by 10.64 on AIGIBench and 17.41 on Chameleon.
icml-2026-fiser-fine-grained-source-repr.tldr: FiSeR improves cross-domain synthetic-image detection by learning both real-versus-generated distinctions and differences among image generators.

paragraphs: FusionCell predicts the delay and power of standard cells, the reusable building blocks of digital circuits. Characterizing these cells through simulation sweeps is slow. Fast predictors can overlook effects arising from physical layout, so this paper combines the geometry of routed layouts with the connectivity described by a circuit’s netlist.

A DeiT encoder processes three-layer layout images, while a graph transformer processes a heterogeneous graph of devices and nets. The model joins these representations through topology-guided attention: connectivity information queries relevant regions of the physical layout. This makes the relationship between circuit structure and physical placement part of the prediction process.

The authors construct an ASAP7-based 7nm dataset containing over 19,500 cells across 149 types, covering six rise/fall delay, transition, and power metrics. FusionCell reports average percentage error of 0.92%, improved ranking correlations over baselines, and characterization speedups of orders of magnitude relative to simulation. These results support using both modalities to estimate values and compare candidate cells.
icml-2026-fusioncell-cross-attentive-fus.tldr: FusionCell combines circuit connectivity with physical layout to predict standard-cell performance accurately and much faster than simulation.

paragraphs: GenUnfold predicts how the force required to unfold a protein changes as the molecule extends. Measuring these trajectories experimentally is costly and time-consuming. The paper develops a scalable diffusion framework for generating full trajectories and establishes a systematic benchmark using a biomolecule stretching database and representative existing models.

The model combines evolutionary context with a local representation of protein mechanics. A physics-biased attention mechanism models dependencies between residues using both structural connections and interaction stiffness. This guides trajectory generation with information about the protein’s mechanical organization as well as its evolutionary relationships.

The authors report reductions in distributional error measured by FID of 30% versus pretrained ESM-2 and 54% versus a standard transformer. In downstream prediction, errors for unfolding force and energy distributions decrease by 6% and 36% relative to ESM-2. These findings support improvements in both curve similarity and physical consistency. The proposed application is screening proteins for promising mechanical properties before costly physical validation, with potential relevance to force-targeted therapeutics.
icml-2026-genunfold-rapidly-predict-prot.tldr: GenUnfold combines protein evolution and mechanical structure in a diffusion model that improves predictions of full unfolding-force trajectories.

paragraphs: Geometric problem solving can require alternating between drawing a diagram and making logical deductions. This paper investigates why teaching a multimodal model that alternating format does not necessarily improve reasoning. The authors find that naive supervised fine-tuning on interleaved plots and solutions substantially reduces performance relative to text-only baselines.

Their explanation is that supervised training can teach the appearance of the workflow without teaching how a plot should influence subsequent deductions. A model may reproduce the expected sequence of drawing and text while failing to use their causal relationship. Faire addresses this with reinforcement learning and three constraints intended to make plotting functionally connected to reasoning.

Experiments report a qualitative change in model behavior, with plotting becoming effectively internalized and performance competitive on challenging geometry benchmarks. The result supports the paper’s distinction between reproducing an interleaved format and learning to use it productively. Its contribution is a training framework aimed at making visual construction serve the reasoning process, rather than assuming that interleaved examples alone achieve that connection.
icml-2026-how-rl-unlocks-the-aha-moment-.tldr: Faire uses reinforcement learning to connect plotting with geometric reasoning after naive interleaved supervised training degrades performance.

paragraphs: Hyperbolic metric learning represents relationships in a geometry suited to hierarchical data. Most previous work has used the Poincaré model, whose shortest paths are curved. This paper investigates the Klein model, where those paths are straight, arguing that this structure aligns more naturally with the linear projections widely used in neural-network feature transformations.

The challenge is making that geometry workable during optimization. The authors formalize a framework using Einstein gyrovector operations and derive a numerically stable metric-learning method. This addresses optimization difficulties inherent to the Klein model while allowing its geometric properties to shape the learned representation.

Experiments on multiple image datasets examine fine-grained classification, where representations must distinguish closely related categories. The Klein approach delivers highly competitive performance without increasing parameter complexity. These empirical findings establish it as a viable alternative to the Poincaré model and support its use as an efficient geometric prior. The claim is about the demonstrated usefulness of this geometry, rather than universal superiority across all metric-learning problems.
icml-2026-klein-hyperbolic-metric-learni.tldr: The paper makes Klein-model hyperbolic metric learning numerically stable and demonstrates competitive fine-grained classification without additional parameters.

paragraphs: Structure-based RNA design seeks sequences that can fold into a specified three-dimensional shape. The paper identifies scarce annotations, noisy structures, and complex RNA geometry as major challenges. It also argues that fixed nearest-neighbor graphs and rigid information-passing rules inadequately represent the flexible, heterogeneous relationships within RNA structures.

ATL-FGD addresses representation and knowledge transfer together. Adaptive Topology Learning uses differentiable gates on graph edges, allowing connections and features to be learned jointly. The resulting graph can change across layers according to the data. FiLM-Guided Distillation then uses feature-wise linear modulation to connect structural and sequence representations, transferring knowledge from RNA foundation models.

The foundation models provide knowledge during learning without being required at inference. This makes their sequence information available to the design framework without adding that dependency when generating sequences. Experiments report significant improvements in sequence recovery and structural fidelity. Together, these findings support combining learned structural relationships with transferred sequence knowledge for more robust RNA design.
icml-2026-learning-adaptive-topology-wit.tldr: ATL-FGD combines adaptive structural graphs with distilled RNA foundation-model knowledge to improve sequence recovery and structural fidelity.

paragraphs: Benchmark compression selects a small set of evaluation questions whose results can estimate performance on the full benchmark. Existing methods often learn which questions are representative from correctness patterns across many previously evaluated models. That approach becomes statistically unstable when few source models are available, a particularly relevant problem for newly released benchmarks.

RepCore uses hidden representations to obtain more information from each source model than a correct-or-incorrect label provides. It aligns heterogeneous hidden states into a shared latent space and uses that space to choose representative subsets. Performance on those subsets is then extrapolated to estimate full-benchmark results.

Across five benchmarks and more than 200 models, the authors report consistent improvements in estimation accuracy and model-ranking correlation over output-based baselines. Accurate estimation is reported with as few as ten source models. Spectral analysis also suggests that the aligned representations separate broad response tendencies from task-specific reasoning patterns, helping explain why internal features can support informative subset selection with limited evaluation history.
icml-2026-learning-more-from-less-unlock.tldr: RepCore uses aligned model hidden states to select compact benchmark subsets, improving performance estimates with few source models.

paragraphs: Crowdsourced datasets often collect several labels for each example because individual non-expert annotators can make mistakes. Repetition improves the available evidence but can also waste effort, both by collecting unnecessary labels for one example and by repeatedly annotating very similar examples. MA³S decides where additional annotation is most useful as labels arrive.

The method estimates uncertainty for each instance with a margin-Beta distribution and updates that estimate online. It also builds a nearest-neighbor graph to propagate uncertainty between related examples. These two mechanisms address different sources of redundancy: outdated annotation decisions and failure to account for similarity across the dataset.

Selection depends only on the estimated uncertainties, without requiring feedback from a predictive model. This makes the strategy independent of a particular model’s training process while remaining responsive to new labels. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets report consistent improvements over existing annotation strategies. The contribution is a coordinated way to allocate repeated annotation using both evolving evidence and relationships among examples.
icml-2026-ma-3-s-model-agnostic-active-a.tldr: MA³S allocates repeated crowdsourced labeling using online uncertainty estimates and example similarity, without predictive-model feedback.

paragraphs: This paper asks what downstream accuracy is attainable for a given pretraining compute budget under contemporary post-training practice. It estimates capability boundaries from observational model evaluations, focusing on high conditional quantiles of benchmark performance. These boundaries describe the stronger observed outcomes associated with compute levels, rather than the performance every model should achieve.

Using 5,000 observational and 2,000 newly sampled data points, the authors fit smooth, monotone, saturating curves against log pretraining FLOPs. They test temporal reliability by fitting earlier model generations and evaluating later releases. Most task boundaries remain broadly stable, while the math-reasoning boundary advances consistently over time.

The analysis also examines task-dependent saturation and contamination-related shifts in math reasoning. An evaluation algorithm recovers frontiers close to those obtained from the full dataset using roughly 20% of the evaluation budget. Alongside the Proteus-2k dataset, the work offers a practical method for setting compute-based performance expectations and detecting when those expectations change as modeling practice evolves.
icml-2026-prescriptive-scaling-reveals-t.tldr: Observational capability curves are mostly stable across model generations, while math reasoning improves at comparable pretraining compute.

paragraphs: Distilling a powerful reasoning model into a smaller student can reduce inference cost, but supervision designed for ordinary fine-tuning can conflict with reinforcement learning. Fixed teacher examples may poorly match the student’s changing outputs. A separate teacher-student divergence penalty can also compete with reward maximization, requiring careful balancing between imitation and task improvement.

RL-aware distillation makes imitation conditional on whether it helps the current policy update. Its Trust Region Ratio Distillation component replaces the usual KL penalty with a likelihood-ratio objective in the style of PPO or GRPO. The objective uses a mixture of the teacher and the student’s old policy as its anchor and operates on student-generated rollouts.

This construction makes distillation sensitive to advantages while bounding updates within a trust region. The authors describe it as balancing exploration, exploitation, and imitation within the policy-learning procedure. Across logic and mathematics benchmarks, RLAD consistently outperforms offline distillation, standard GRPO, and KL-based on-policy distillation, supporting the value of adapting teacher guidance to the student’s ongoing learning.
icml-2026-reinforcement-aware-knowledge-.tldr: RLAD selectively integrates teacher imitation into reinforcement-learning updates and improves reasoning over several distillation and RL baselines.

paragraphs: Language models can translate a natural-language optimization problem into executable solver code, but successful execution does not establish that the code expresses the intended problem. A model can contain logically incorrect constraints or objectives without triggering a solver error. SAC-Opt targets these semantic mistakes, which limited post-hoc debugging can leave undetected.

The framework repeatedly compares semantic anchors from the original problem with anchors reconstructed from the generated code. It then corrects only the components whose meanings do not match. This backward comparison directs refinement toward the intended constraints and objective, making the original problem description an explicit reference throughout correction.

SAC-Opt requires no additional training or supervision. On seven public datasets, the authors report an average modeling-accuracy improvement of 7.7%, with gains reaching 21.9% on ComplexLP. The results support iterative checks of meaning as a useful complement to executable-code generation. The central contribution is a targeted correction process that can identify discrepancies even when the solver accepts the program.
icml-2026-sac-opt-semantic-anchors-for-i.tldr: SAC-Opt improves generated optimization models by repeatedly checking their recovered meaning against the original problem and correcting mismatches.

paragraphs: scChord infers single-cell protein abundance from RNA measurements, addressing the expense and throughput constraints of direct protein measurement. The paper argues that deterministic constraints on noisy data can distort the geometry of a learned representation. When measurement variability differs across observations, forcing that uncertainty into fixed latent relationships can make learning unstable.

The framework combines conditional flow matching with a probabilistic decoder. The decoder represents technical noise and over-dispersion through distributional parameters, allowing the latent representation to focus more on biological signals. This probabilistic rectification provides a more regular geometry for learning the transport trajectories used in prediction.

Experiments across multiple multi-omics benchmarks report state-of-the-art inference accuracy, alongside faithful reconstruction of biological heterogeneity and complex protein distributions. These findings address both prediction quality and the preservation of variation across cells. The approach matters because uncertainty is treated as something to represent explicitly, reducing the pressure for noisy measurements to determine the shape of the biological latent space.
icml-2026-scchord-a-probabilistic-manifo.tldr: scChord separates measurement noise from biological latent structure to improve protein-abundance inference from single-cell RNA data.

paragraphs: SCRWKV addresses crack segmentation, where accurate pixel labels must preserve thin structural patterns despite complex textures and interference. The paper focuses on the difficulty of modeling crack topology while keeping resource requirements low. Its proposed network uses a Structure-Field Encoder with linear computational complexity to combine structural reasoning with a compact model.

Inside the encoder, a multiscale modulator strengthens texture representations. A structure-calibrated unit uses geometry-guided bidirectional transformations to capture topological relationships, while a dynamic decay mechanism suppresses the propagation of noise. A lightweight cross-scale decoder then aggregates the resulting features into a segmentation prediction.

The network contains 1.22 million parameters. Across multiple challenging benchmarks, the authors report significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods, including an F1 score of 0.8428 and mIoU of 0.8512 on TUT. These results support the potential for efficient deployment while retaining strong segmentation quality. The contribution is the coordinated treatment of texture, structural connectivity, and noise within a small linear-complexity architecture.
icml-2026-scrwkv-ultra-compact-structure.tldr: SCRWKV combines structural modeling and noise control in a 1.22-million-parameter network for efficient crack segmentation.

paragraphs: Multimodal alignment can deteriorate when deployment changes the distributions of individual modalities, even if useful relationships between them persist. SSCA targets dependence that remains stable under approximately coordinate-wise monotone distortions. This is a specific shift setting: the protocol aims to preserve cross-modal relationships while reducing sensitivity to changes in individual feature distributions.

The method first uses clipped soft ranks and Gaussianization to suppress marginal effects while tracking approximation and tie errors. It then couples modalities through a shared hub using dependence-weighted sliced Wasserstein alignment. A stabilized spectral learning stage adds diagnostics for the risk that the learned subspace changes, and cycle auditing checks multiway consistency.

A calibrated gate converts these diagnostics into a reliability signal with measurable false-alarm and miss trade-offs. That signal supports stability updates, budgeted remediation, or a conservative no-update response to out-of-scope drift. Evaluations on MOSEI/MELD, MSCOCO, and CC3M-500K report better perturbation performance and reduced degradation across controlled distortions, pipeline drifts, and frozen-feature retrieval tests.
icml-2026-stable-spectral-copula-alignme.tldr: SSCA combines shift-resistant multimodal alignment with label-free diagnostics that guide updates and fallback under deployment drift.

paragraphs: Binary segmentation metrics determine how predicted foreground regions are judged against reference masks. Pixel-based scores such as IoU and Dice can miss structural damage because their statistics do not directly describe connectivity or fragmentation. The paper also identifies weaknesses in S-measure, including sensitivity to small objects, background false positives, and critical structural violations.

T-measure combines three complementary components. A Fuzzy Jaccard score provides the foundational comparison. A topological integrity term penalizes important structural fragmentation, while a boundary alignment term assesses how well predicted borders match the reference. Together, these components aim to account for both regional agreement and the organization of the predicted shape.

The authors introduce a Meta-Measure validation framework and compare T-measure with nine mainstream metrics across complex scenarios. They report strong downstream performance and high agreement with human visual perception. The contribution is an evaluation criterion that explicitly incorporates topology, making structural integrity part of the score used to assess segmentation quality rather than relying entirely on pixel-level agreement.
icml-2026-t-measure-a-topology-consisten.tldr: T-measure evaluates binary segmentation using regional agreement, structural integrity, and boundary alignment to better reflect perceived quality.

paragraphs: Radiology report generators often learn multiple tasks to combine fluent reporting with clinically consistent predictions. This paper argues that simple weighted combinations of task losses inadequately balance discriminative clinical supervision with the smoother learning requirements of text generation. It studies the problem through gradient dynamics, rather than introducing another reporting architecture.

Using a stochastic differential equation framework, the authors describe two failures: deviation of the drift term and decay of the diffusion term. CAME-Grad addresses them by adjusting gradient directions to reduce conflict and enhancing gradient magnitude. An adaptive fusion mechanism then balances the theoretically preferred direction with the inductive biases contributed by individual tasks.

The optimizer can be added to different model backbones. Across eight radiology report generation methods, the authors report substantial, consistent gains, with average clinical-efficacy improvements of 2.3% on MIMIC-CXR and 1.9% on IU X-Ray. These findings suggest that how task gradients are combined is an important intervention point for improving report generation, alongside the choice of model architecture.
icml-2026-the-double-dilemma-in-multi-ta.tldr: CAME-Grad adjusts conflicting task gradients and their magnitudes, improving clinical efficacy across eight radiology report generation methods.

paragraphs: UniFast-HGR targets the computational burden of learning dependence between high-dimensional modalities using maximal correlation. It is a scalable surrogate for the Hirschfeld–Gebelein–Rényi objective. The design retains paired dependence maximization and the covariance-control role of Soft-HGR while changing how the necessary relationships are estimated within a training batch.

The method replaces explicit covariance whitening with centered, length-normalized cosine alignment. It uses an identity linking covariance and Gram-matrix traces to form a local-batch structural objective, then removes invariant diagonal self-correlations through Trivial Spectrum Suppression. Its dominant structural cost is O(m²K), where m is local batch size and K is feature dimension. An additional variant uses stochastic projection to reduce practical memory requirements.

Experiments cover retrieval, image classification, remote sensing segmentation, and multimodal emotion recognition. The authors report consistent gains over covariance-based HGR/CCA variants and contrastive or neural mutual-information objectives on strong backbones. Microbenchmarks also show stable behavior at extreme feature dimensions, supporting the approach as a practical dependence-learning objective for large multimodal representations.
icml-2026-unifast-hgr-scalable-and-effic.tldr: UniFast-HGR reformulates maximal-correlation learning around local-batch operations to improve scalability and multimodal task performance.

paragraphs: UniJEPA explores how generalist robot policies can combine semantic understanding with predictions about visual change. Prior approaches commonly build on either vision-language models or generative models. The paper argues that robots can benefit from both forms of pretraining knowledge, bringing understanding, planning, and continuous future representations into the same policy-learning approach.

The model first learns to dynamically represent high-dimensional visual features from more than one million internet instructional manipulation videos. It is then fine-tuned using data from the robot embodiment. This second stage connects predictive representations to discrete action tokens, translating information about visual futures into actions suited to the robot.

The authors report consistent improvements over baselines, with gains of 9% in simulation environments and 12% on real-world out-of-distribution tasks. The findings support the proposed combination of continuous predictive learning and discrete action generation in the evaluated settings. The contribution is a route from broad video pretraining to embodiment-specific control that draws on both visual dynamics and semantic understanding.
icml-2026-unijepa-enhancing-robot-policy.tldr: UniJEPA learns predictive visual representations from manipulation videos and maps them to robot actions, improving simulated and real-world performance.

paragraphs: This paper investigates which properties make generated images useful for training segmentation models. Photorealism alone does not explain how synthetic data supports detailed spatial understanding, so the authors systematically analyze images produced by modern diffusion models. Their focus is the relationship between synthetic scene characteristics and the representations learned for segmentation.

The analysis identifies dense scene composition and fidelity of individual instances as especially beneficial. Images with these properties produce more discriminative spatial representations, helping models learn distinctions relevant to segmentation. Building on those findings, the authors introduce SENSE, a unified framework that uses flexible, scalable synthetic data to improve segmentation performance.

SENSE is model-agnostic and works with architectures including DPT and Mask2Former, as well as models with different parameter capacities. Experiments on Cityscapes, COCO, and ADE20K support its effectiveness and generalization. The contribution combines an explanation of useful synthetic-data properties with a framework for exploiting them, connecting data design to spatial representation quality across several segmentation settings.
icml-2026-what-makes-synthetic-data-effe.tldr: SENSE uses synthetic images with dense scenes and faithful instances to improve segmentation across architectures and model sizes.
